#ekyavanaearlyyears #learningbynature #preschool #manyata #haralur

At Ekya Vana Early Years, we believe a child’s learning journey should begin amongst nature.

Before screens, there should be soil beneath their feet.
Before simulations, there should be something real to touch, smell, hear and feel.
Before consuming, there should be creating.
Before answers, there should be curiosity and questioning.

Our children plant, water, dig, build, paint, play, observe, make, share and care.

They learn through their hands.
Through all their senses.
Through play.
Through nature-led methods.
Through one another.

Because the early years are about how children experience the world, how they relate to it, and who they become within it.

And that is something we will always make space for.

Therefore, AI could never! 🌱

#ekyavanaearlyyears #learningbynature #purposebasedschool #natureledlearning #preschool

What do you want to be when you grow up?

At Ekya Vana Early Years, in a world where children are increasingly shaped to become consumers, we nurture them to become creators: children who question, imagine and make..

Through play, collaboration, curiosity and empathy, children develop a sense of agency - the confidence to make choices and take action in their lives.

They develop a willingness to care for one another and the natural world. 

Because the world needs children who don’t just consume what already exists, but children who shape what comes next.

What helps children stay focused, curious and confident? 

Sometimes, it’s a teacher who knows when to guide, when to step back, and when to simply be there.

At Ekya Vana Early Years, our trained educators build relationships rooted in kindness, patience and trust. They gently guide children through each step, giving them the confidence to explore, make choices and learn at their own pace.

And somewhere along the way, teachers become more than educators: they become trusted friends, companions and co-explorers.

Because when children feel safe, seen and supported, learning unfolds naturally.

Here, nature leads and wonderful relationships help children grow. 🌱

‘They’re just playing.’

But what if play is how children learn to think, create, connect and grow?

At Ekya Vana Early Years, we believe that play is not a break from learning. Play IS learning. And when nature leads the way, every experience becomes an opportunity to discover.

🌿 What does play nurture?

• Curiosity & problem-solving: Asking questions, experimenting and finding their own answers.

• Social-emotional learning: Sharing, collaborating, communicating and learning to navigate big feelings.

• Creativity & imagination: Turning a stick into a wand, a mud kitchen into a restaurant and an idea into something new.

• Literacy & language: Building stories, learning new words, expressing ideas and discovering the joy of communication.

• Numeracy & logical thinking: Counting natural treasures, comparing sizes, recognising patterns and understanding quantities through real experiences.

• Confidence & independence: Making choices, taking small risks and learning through trial and error.

🌱 And when nature meets play?

Children don’t just learn about the world. They learn WITH the natural world.

A walk becomes a lesson in observation. A fallen leaf becomes a discovery. A puddle becomes an experiment. A garden becomes a space to wonder, question, and grow.

Because childhood is not about rushing towards the next milestone. It is about giving children the time, space and freedom to learn in ways that come naturally to them.

Where Nature Leads, and Play Unfolds. 

That’s the Ekya Vana way. 💛

What happens when learning begins with water, wonder, and tiny living beings? 💧

At our Bio Pond Workshop at RMV, our students and their parents stepped into a world of fish, frogs, dragonflies, snails, stones, leaves, and endless little discoveries.

They learnt why fresh water matters, who calls a pond home, and how we can become Bio Pond Helpers - using gentle hands, keeping water bodies clean, and caring for every living being around us.

Then came the sensory exploration.

Feeling the water.
Holding stones.
Touching leaves.
Counting fish.
Watching a fish hide beneath the leaves.
Noticing its colour.
And learning to look a little closer.

For one little explorer, the pond became a world to investigate: counting the fish again and again, recognising their colours, and excitedly spotting where they had disappeared!

Parents, too, learnt how to create and care for natural ponds at home, turning everyday spaces into habitats for life.

Because at Ekya Vana, learning isn’t only about knowing nature.
It is about feeling connected to it, caring for it, and understanding our place within it.

A little water.
A lot of wonder.
And the beginnings of a deeper People & Planet and EarthCare connection. 🌱

What if, before we teach children to notice the world, we learn to notice it ourselves? 🌿

At the launch of Ekya Vana Early Years, Manyata, our fireside chat brought together Gagan Saiprasad of Mycelium Ecology and Kavya Chandra of A Green Venture Nature Walks, to explore something beautifully simple: Observation.

Children and their parents don’t always need more things to do. Sometimes, they need us to slow down, unlearn, and look closely.

A nature walk can become a lesson in patience.
A leaf can become a story to document.
A tiny caterpillar can become a months-long journey: from caterpillar to cocoon to butterfly (or moth), and finally, watching it fly away.

At Ekya Vana, we believe early learning begins with this kind of wonder - not rushing to answers, but making space to observe, question, connect and care.

Because sometimes, the most meaningful learning happens when we simply stop and look. 🌱
